title: 02. Data Structures: Linear Recursion on Arrays & Lists
summary: Linear Recursion on Arrays = Process one element at a time, recursing on the rest.

sections.title: EXPLANATION
sections.body:
**Linear Recursion on Arrays** = Process one element at a time, recursing on the rest.

Pattern:
```python
def process(arr, index=0):
    if index == len(arr):    # BASE CASE: past the end
        return base_value
    # Process arr[index]
    return combine(arr[index], process(arr, index + 1))
```

This is the **most fundamental pattern** for recursive list processing. Once you master this, tree recursion and backtracking feel natural.

quiz.explanation: 5yr Answer: Two patterns: 1) Index-based: pass the array unchanged + a current index (process(arr, i)). Memory efficient since same array is referenced. 2) Slice-based: pass progressively smaller slices (process(arr[1:])).

quiz.question: What is the time and space complexity of recursive array processing?
options: 5-Year Experience Answer: > The Recursive Leap of Faith means: assume your recursive function works correctly for smaller inputs, and use that assumption to solve the current problem.
Memoization is top-down: start with the original problem, recurse, cache results as you go (lazy — only compute what's needed).
Memory efficient since same array is referenced.
This is the same time as iteration but WORSE space (iteration is O(1) space).
quiz.explanation: 5yr Answer: For LINEAR recursion on an array of n elements: Time O(n) — each element processed once. Space O(n) — n stack frames. This is the same time as iteration but WORSE space (iteration is O(1) space).

options: 5-Year Experience Answer: > The core problem with tree recursion is that the SAME subproblems get computed multiple times. fib(30) computes fib(15) thousands of times…

5yr Answer: Always handle them in the BASE CASE. Empty array is the most common base case (if not arr: return 0).
quiz.explanation: 5yr Answer: Always handle them in the BASE CASE. Empty array is the most common base case (if not arr: return 0). Single element is sometimes also a base case (if len(arr) == 1: return arr[0]).

quiz.question: What is the difference between processing from left-to-right vs right-to-left in recursive array processing?
options: Also, infinite recursion if base case is wrong or missing.
Memory efficient since same array is referenced.
5yr Answer: Pruning means cutting off branches of the search tree that CANNOT lead to valid solutions.
5yr Answer: Left-to-right: process(arr[0]) + recurse(arr[1:]) — processes first element NOW, recurses on the rest.
quiz.explanation: 5yr Answer: Left-to-right: process(arr[0]) + recurse(arr[1:]) — processes first element NOW, recurses on the rest. Right-to-left: recurse(arr[:-1]) + process(arr[-1]) OR use head recursion style where processing happens after return. The ORDER matters for non-commutative operations like string concatenation. [a] + reverse(rest) gives forward order while reverse(rest) + [a] gives backward.
